page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering a balanced configuration of compute and system memory. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache. It is provisioned with 16 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or bundled local storage, relying on external block storage services for persistent data.

Benchmark data indicates exceptional single-core processing capabilities. The instance scores in the top tier for single-core execution in stress-ng and Geekbench 6, as well as single-threaded compression workloads such as gzip and bzip3. However, multi-core throughput aligns with median expectations due to its two-physical-core configuration. Memory performance exhibits high throughput on cached 16 KB read blocks, but uncached large-block (256 MB) reads and writes show reduced bandwidth, resulting in lower scores on database operation benchmarks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4d-standard-4 delivers efficient compute economics for workloads driven by per-thread responsiveness rather than heavy memory streaming. It is well-fitted for web application serving, CI/CD pipeline execution, API routing, and lightweight Redis caching, but is less optimal for I/O-intensive databases or large-scale data transformation.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor, paired with 16 GB of RAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers exceptional single-core compute performance, placing in the top percentiles for single-threaded compression and Geekbench execution. The instance contains no integrated GPU or bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for disk operations. While cached memory transactions are fast, sustained large-block uncached memory bandwidth falls into lower percentiles, impacting heavy database transactional performance. Consequently, n4d-standard-4 offers balanced cost efficiency for tasks prioritizing CPU clock responsiveness over wide memory concurrency, making it suitable for web application hosting, microservices, lightweight Redis caching, and code compilation pipelines.
